external_sources.role: host/boot/application-specific identity and machine-readable login/session inspection
virtualization/device-emulation comparator; simulation cannot establish exact physical-host identity

source_findings: systemd documents /etc/machine-id as stable across subsequent boots and independent of local/network configuration or hardware replacement; therefore it is useful as an installation lineage input but cannot by itself prove exact current hardware identity.

systemd explicitly classifies the raw machine ID as confidential and says it must not be exposed directly to untrusted environments. Application-specific machine IDs should be derived irreversibly; sd_id128_get_machine_app_specific() uses an application-specific derivation built from HMAC-SHA256 semantics.

systemd exposes a boot ID that changes per running kernel instance, and separate invocation/session identity surfaces. Stable host lineage, boot epoch, service invocation and desktop/login session are therefore distinct scopes and should not be collapsed into one fingerprint.

loginctl provides machine-readable show-session/show-user properties, supporting explicit desktop/login-session proof obligations rather than inferring them from a live process or environment variable alone.

QEMU/KVM provides valuable userspace, lifecycle and fault-surface testing, but emulated/passthrough devices and approximated CPU/device models do not establish silicon/firmware/peripheral identity of the final Minisforum host. SIMULATED_HOST_VERIFIED must remain below EXACT_HOST_BOUND.

hw-probe demonstrates the breadth possible in hardware inventory, but its normal workflow can collect logs, use elevated access, and upload an anonymized probe. That is materially broader than F2-WP-1201's privacy-bounded read-only identity need; its own README notes anonymization may fail in edge cases.
The strongest F2 design is therefore a thin native allowlisted collector, not importing a broad inventory/upload framework.

identity_model.host_scope_id: application-specific derived machine identifier; never persist/export raw /etc/machine-id
identity_model.boot_scope_id: boot-specific identifier kept separate from host_scope_id
identity_model.session_or_invocation_scope: explicit login/session/service invocation identity when the requirement depends on it
identity_model.profile_generation_digest: deterministic digest over an allowlisted canonical projection of observed technical facts plus explicit UNKNOWN states

minimum_rules: Separate stable installation/host lineage from mutable hardware/capability profile; a stable host_scope_id must not mask hardware or driver changes.
Never collect or persist raw serial numbers, MAC addresses, raw machine-id, credentials, clipboard, user documents, raw camera frames or raw microphone audio in the baseline fingerprint.
If a requirement truly needs stable per-device continuity, derive a local application-scoped pseudonymous identifier and keep raw identifiers outside receipts/export surfaces.

Every probe is read-only by default, independently timeout-bounded, records command/tool/version/status/provenance, and maps unavailable/permission-denied/parse-failed to typed UNKNOWN rather than false/pass.
Bind host-specific evidence to profile generation/digest and boot scope where relevant; profile changes stale dependent host evidence instead of silently reusing it.
Represent virtualization/twin identity explicitly. Simulated profiles can support SIMULATED_HOST_VERIFIED but can never satisfy EXACT_HOST_BOUND or REAL_READBACK_VERIFIED for the physical target.
Prefer requirement-specific probe bundles over one ever-growing global fingerprint so privacy, churn and invalidation scope remain bounded.

counterhypotheses: A very detailed host fingerprint may cause needless invalidation from benign changes and may become a privacy liability; a coarser stable identity plus requirement-specific capability proofs may be superior.

Application-specific machine identity still follows /etc/machine-id semantics and therefore does not prove unchanged hardware; hardware-sensitive acceptance must depend on the mutable profile digest and direct capability/readback evidence, not host_scope_id alone.

A broad inventory tool could reduce implementation effort, but its dependency, privilege, collection and upload surface may exceed the small deterministic F2 acceptance contract and obscure exact evidence provenance.
next_falsifier: For the F2-WP-1201 implementation, test deterministic profile behavior across repeated same-boot runs, reboot, benign package/tool-version change, kernel/driver change, USB hotplug/removal, missing permissions, VM/container execution and synthetic hardware change. Verify forbidden raw identifiers never enter output; verify required profile changes invalidate dependent host evidence while stable host lineage remains separate.
architecture_delta: E1 supports a candidate split between HostScopeIdentity, BootScopeIdentity and TargetEnvironmentProfileDigest, plus requirement-specific HostCapabilityWitnesses. E2 mapping is required before architecture credit or Trigger-4 handoff.
